clue.text: Salad ingredient right with one kind of food

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
a dish is a kind of food prepared for a meal

explanation.surface: A recipe note about a salad component served alongside a particular dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp red root vegetable commonly sliced raw into salads, an example of the category.

clue.text: Crowd of people with wine bag

parts.note: a ruck is a dense crowd or jostling throng of people
sack is an old name for a dry white fortified wine like sherry

explanation.surface: A gathering of people carrying wine in a bag, as at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK, the old fortified wine Falstaff drank, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a bag carried on the back, a specific type of bag for walkers.

clue.text: Tribesman's level of fighting skill

definitions.meaning: a member of one of the twelve tribes of Israel, the tribe descended from Jacob's son of this name
a grade of proficiency in judo or karate, as in a black belt's first grade

explanation.surface: A remark about the martial arts grading of a member of some tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Dan names both an Israelite tribe (so one of its men) and a numbered grade of expertise in martial arts.

clue.text: Extra benefit of using faster deliveries only?

definitions.text: Extra benefit of using faster deliveries only?

parts.words: Extra benefit of using faster deliveries only?
parts.note: in cricket a captain who uses only fast bowlers has taken the slow turning bowlers out of the attack, so that kind of bowling is switched off; read as one phrase it is a secondary benefit

explanation.surface: A business question about the bonus of choosing express shipping alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket bowlers are either fast or spinners; using only quick ones means no spin at all. 'Deliveries' are balls bowled, not parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-product or incidental advantage arising from a main activity is called this hyphenated noun.

clue.text: Made peaceful gesture, unfortunately rebuffed by American editor

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word for unfortunately is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Someone offered a gesture of peace, but sadly an American editor turned it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' reads as part of the surface story but is the word to be turned round; a salaam is a deep bow of greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To salaam is to greet with a low bow and hand to forehead, an eastern gesture whose name means peace.

clue.text: Bill is not out of order, twice gathering volunteers for military positions

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: gathering means the doubled piece takes another piece inside it
twice means the jumbled letters appear two times
out of order means the letters of is not are jumbled

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill is ruled in order, while volunteers gather for military duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill is not out of order' sounds like a parliamentary ruling; the Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the order calling troops to their assigned battle posts, the positions themselves.

clue.text: American city worker breaking world record, almost

indicators.note: breaking means one piece bursts into the middle of another
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps, a record of the world
the ant is the classic crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: An American city labourer smashes a world record, or nearly does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'World record' is not a sporting record but a book of maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia, an example of an American city.

clue.text: Calculating behaviour producing new issue

definitions.meaning: working out a product of numbers, a form of arithmetic
breeding offspring, issue meaning children, as creatures do when they increase in number

explanation.surface: A remark that scheming conduct leads to fresh trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplying means both doing times-table arithmetic and reproducing, increasing numbers by breeding.

clue.text: Hold back time's destruction

parts.note: to dam is to hold back water
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A rueful line about trying to resist the ravages of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is harm or ruin done to something, a close synonym of destruction.

clue.text: The kind of assurance oth ers can't have

definitions.text: The kind of assurance oth ers can't have

parts.words: The kind of assurance oth ers can't have
parts.note: the assurance in question belongs to oneself by definition, so nobody else can possess it for you

explanation.surface: A remark about some kind of guarantee unavailable to other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text splits 'others' as 'oth ers'. 'Assurance' sounds like insurance cover but means confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: This is belief in one's own abilities, an assurance that by its name rests in oneself alone.

clue.text: European innocent disturbed by gossip mostly

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of innocent are stirred up
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: talk is idle chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: A guileless European is rattled by rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges INNOCENT to CONTINEN; 'mostly' trims TALK to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To Britons, continental means of mainland Europe, so a person from there; a British usage.

clue.text: Beat innocent child soundly

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a lamb is a meek, innocent person, especially a child

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes a blameless youngster thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but says that the word is heard: LAMB, silent B, gives LAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is a slang verb meaning to thrash or hit hard.

clue.text: Who's an exhibitionist?

parts.note: the letters of the word who's, rearranged, spell a word meaning display; with the anagram signal off after them they make the wordplay

explanation.surface: A simple question asking which person is a flamboyant exhibitionist.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay is SHOW with OFF signalling an anagram, which gives WHOS, the clue's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who flaunts themselves to attract attention is an exhibitionist.

clue.text: Evil tendency that's common in first offence?

parts.note: original means first, from the origin
a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: A theological question about whether the first wrongdoing makes evil universal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The definition says this tendency is common to all humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian doctrine holds that all people inherit a tendency to sin from Adam's fall, an evil shared by all.

clue.text: Sound from pen — love using one

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
using a pen, the one mentioned, means putting ink on paper

explanation.surface: A writer describes the noise of a fountain pen while using one with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is a pigpen, not a writing pen; 'one' refers back to a pen in its writing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the grunting noise pigs make, and pigs are kept in a pen.

clue.text: Police officer catches noble if going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters fall out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A police officer arrests an aristocrat in case anything goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges all of CATCHES NOBLE IF.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the head of a regional police force holds this title, a senior police officer.

clue.text: Setback that won't affect Mum or Dad

definitions.meaning: a misfortune or check to progress

definitions.text: that won't affect Mum or Dad
definitions.meaning: mum and dad read the same backwards, so turning them round changes nothing

explanation.surface: A family misfortune that leaves the parents unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a sudden change for the worse, and also turning letters backwards, which leaves palindromes intact.

clue.text: Time of earliest garden plant

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, time served
Paradise is the Garden of Eden, the first garden

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a period from the very first plot on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD for prison time comes from rhyming slang, 'bird lime'.
explanation.definitionFit: The strelitzia, a crane-flower with a beak-like bloom, is commonly called this, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Fly seen around decomposed bits in this?

definitions.text: Fly seen around decomposed bits in this?

indicators.note: seen around means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a dun is a mayfly, a fly used by anglers

indicators.note: decomposed means the letters of bits are broken up

explanation.surface: Flies buzz round rotting scraps inside a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: A dun is an angler's name for a mayfly; the whole clue also describes the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish container where rotting scraps attract flies, described by the whole clue.

clue.text: Consultant is interrupting part of speech endlessly

indicators.note: interrupting means one piece cuts into the middle of another
endlessly means the final letter is removed

parts.note: an adverb is a part of speech, such as quickly

explanation.surface: A consultant breaks into a grammar lesson that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops only the final letter of the grammatical term before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is someone who gives professional advice, a synonym of adviser.

clue.text: Gift of money no longer usable

definitions.meaning: an ancient unit of weight and currency in Greece and the Middle East, long obsolete

explanation.surface: A present of cash that can no longer be spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent means a natural gift and also the ancient monetary unit of the Bible's parable of the talents.

clue.text: Put together a ship to enter a big sea

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean, a big sea
SS is the steamship prefix

explanation.surface: Instructions to sail a vessel into a large sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Med, short for the Mediterranean, is a crossword staple for a big sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassed means gathered or accumulated, put together in a collection.

clue.text: At very old and good university, English is fashionable

parts.note: in can mean at, as in at home or in

explanation.surface: At a venerable, fine university, English literature is all the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means currently popular or stylish, matching fashionable.

clue.text: Extremes of militarism in

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Extremes of militarism in (3)': the outer letters of militarism are two Ms, giving EMS by sound, but the clue appears cut short after 'in' with no definition; no scan and a search found no fuller text.

clue.text: Crazy types abandoned daughter: do they give her the slip?

definitions.text: do they give her the slip?

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy

indicators.note: abandoned means a letter is left out

parts.note: kinds are types or sorts

explanation.surface: Mad people deserted a daughter; are they making her trip up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes D from KINDS. 'Give her the slip' means cause her to slip, not escape her.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded peel from a tropical fruit is the comic cause of slipping, the definition read as a cryptic question.

clue.text: Doctrine happens to go with mass

parts.note: is means exists or takes place, happens
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A belief system that tends to go along with church Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is a distinctive doctrine or ideology, from the suffix of words like socialism.

clue.text: Holding stake, be likely to be occupied

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains another

parts.note: to tend is to be likely, to incline towards
an ante is a stake put into a poker pot

explanation.surface: Someone holding a share in a property expects it to be lived in.
explanation.walkthrough: An ante is a poker player's stake paid in before the cards are dealt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenanted means having tenants living there, so occupied.

clue.text: From the beginning, China protects border

indicators.note: protects means one piece surrounds another

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate, so a pal
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: From the start, the Chinese state has guarded its frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means original or primeval, existing from the very beginning.
